name: first-campaign-regional
about: A carrier with no history: the pack holds the job and the benchmark only.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.

output.audience: Class A drivers who already pull flatbed and meet the experience requirement, living on or near Midwest lanes. They likely run regional or longer now and want a steady week. A plain pay per mile, weekly home time and their own assigned truck would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile for flatbed work on Midwest lanes, shown over a loaded flatbed on the road.
angles.proof: The opening states its pay per mile, and the work is flatbed on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Pay is the plainest fact the job has and a driver can compare it at a glance. Nothing has been measured for this carrier yet, format included, so this is a starting test.

angles.idea: Lead with being home weekly, shown as a quiet street at the end of a regional week.
angles.proof: The opening offers home weekly on regional Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Home time is the job's stated schedule and speaks to drivers out longer than they want. No history says whether it pulls better than pay, and no format has been measured.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck: a parked flatbed rig that is the driver's own to run each week.
angles.proof: The job lists an assigned truck and flatbed equipment.
angles.why: An assigned truck matters to drivers who share equipment now, and a still suits a truck at rest. Untested for this carrier; nothing has been measured about hooks or formats.

angles.idea: Say plainly who this is for: Class A, flatbed, the stated experience, Midwest lanes, seen from the driver's seat.
angles.proof: The job is Class A regional flatbed on Midwest lanes and states an experience requirement.
angles.why: Stating the requirement and the area up front should keep out leads who cannot qualify, which helps against the benchmark pause point. This carrier has no results or format data yet.

angles.idea: Set the job's terms out as a plain list: pay per mile, home weekly, retirement plan, a small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.proof: Each line is a stated fact of the opening, including the carrier's own words about its small fleet.
angles.why: With no history, the listed facts are the only proof this carrier has, and a plain ground lets them be read fast. Nothing has been measured, format included.
